verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. Both clauses are present, but as different objects, and the notation ℒ(z,t) is nowhere introduced. (i) No declaration was found defining a band set {ℓ : (z,t) ∈ 𝒟_ℓ}, nor 𝒟_ℓ as a set of (z,t) (the paper's (6.17) defines it as supp_{(z,t)} χ_ℓ(q(z,t))). The Lean works with full labels L = (band, grid cell, sign): LabelCounting.pointwiseLabels takes q as a free real argument and imposes q ∈ tsupport (dyadicMask L.1) ∧ slowCoordinates D L.1 x ∈ normalizedBox A L, whose first conjunct is the paper's (z,t) ∈ 𝒟_ℓ once q = q(z,t) is substituted; PhysicalWaveSum.labelRegion is the same pair of closed supports as a product set. LabelCountingFinite.bandCandidates is only a five-element superset of the bands meeting a point, used for counting. (ii) The r-independence is a separate definitional lemma, LocalAngularDiagonal.slowQ_physical: physicalQ h w factors through slowPoint w = (t, z), so q sees neither radius nor angle. The purpose the paper puts the display to — that the band set is fixed during radial integration, so Lemma 6.3 bounds the labels met by the integral — is carried in the Lean by LabelCounting.number_of_relevant_labels applied to pointwiseLabels; I did not find a declaration asserting that the set of relevant bands is constant along a radial line.
